newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY WELCOMES ROMANIA ELECTION OUTCOME.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY WELCOMES ROMANIA ELECTION OUTCOME.

text.p: Hungary on Tuesday said it welcomed the fact the most votes in Romania's elections had gone to parties which supported the signing of a friendship treaty between the two countries in September.

The basic treaty, which is essential for the two countries' ambitions to join NATO and the European Union, was aimed at ending a centuries-old rift between the two neighbours by settling the status of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians and guaranteeing Romania's western borders.
Romania went to the polls on Sunday to elect a new parliament and president.

With official results reported from nearly three-quarters of Romania's 15,000 polling stations, the centrist Democratic Convention (CDR) had some 30 percent of the vote, thrashing the ex-Communists of president Ion Iliescu, with 23 percent.

It remained unclear who would emerge as president. Iliescu led a field of 16 in Sunday's voting with 33 percent and went through to a November 17 run-off with the CDR's leader, professor Emil Constantinescu.
Hungarian foreign ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi told a news conference that Hungary wished to develop its relations with the new Romanian government along the principles of the basic treaty.
"The first results of the elections seem to fulfil our hopes in that those parties which supported the basic treaty during the ratification process are ahead," Szentivanyi added.

The spokesman said Hungary hoped that Romania would improve further the situation of its ethnic minorities according to European norms and the principles laid down in the friendship treaty, and that Romania's Euroatlantic integration would continue.
Szentivanyi added that the Hungarian Parliament is likely to ratify the basic treaty by the end of this year.
Parliament postponed ratification of the treaty earlier this month because it did not want to influence the Romanian elections.
Romania ratified the treaty in early October.
